channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Japanese Yen softens after Fed leaves rates on hold
item.description: The USD/JPY pair posts modest gains near 163.50 during the Asian trading hours on Thursday. The US Dollar (USD) strengthens against the Japanese Yen (JPY) on a hawkish hold from the US Federal Reserve (Fed).

item.title: US resumes strikes against Iran, targeting Qeshm Island
item.description: The US Central Command (CENTCOM) began launching strikes against Iran late Wednesday, retaliating against Iranian missile attacks on American forces in the region, the Guardian reported.

item.title: Japan’s Katayama says official proposed no ceiling on next year’s budget requests
item.description: Japan's Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama said that officials proposed no ceiling on next year’s budget requests.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar rises as ANZ Business Outlook Index jumps in July
item.description: NZD/USD extends its gains for the third consecutive day, trading around 0.5810 during the Asian hours on Thursday. The currency pair climbs higher as the New Zealand Dollar (NZD) receives support from a sharp rise in domestic business confidence.

item.title: Canadian Dollar consolidates as Mideast crisis supports oil and USD ahead of US data
item.description: The USD/CAD pair is seen consolidating below mid-1.4000s during the Asian session on Thursday, though it remains close to an over one-week trough touched the previous day.

item.title: WTI falls below $83.00 despite hostilities in the Middle East
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI), the US crude oil benchmark, is trading around $82.80 during the early Asian trading hours on Thursday. WTI falls amid some profit-taking despite escalating conflicts in the Middle East.

item.title: Australian Dollar gains despite cooling domestic Inflation, hawkish Fed hold
item.description: AUD/USD inches higher after two days of losses, trading around 0.6960 during the Asian hours on Thursday. The currency pair may face potential downside pressure as the US Dollar (USD) could gain strength following a hawkish interest rate pause by the Federal Reserve (Fed).

item.title: PBOC sets USD/CNY reference rate at 6.7892 vs. 6.7899 previous
item.description: The People’s Bank of China (PBOC) sets the USD/CNY central rate for the trading session ahead at 6.7892 compared to the previous day's fix of 6.7899.

item.title: British Pound retreats from weekly high vs firmer USD as focus shifts to BoE, US data
item.description: The GBP/USD pair struggles to capitalize on the previous day's strong move up to the weekly high and drifts lower during the Asian session on Thursday.

item.title: Euro edges lower to near 1.1450 as Fed holds rates steady, traders await Eurozone and German GDP
item.description: The EUR/USD pair trades with mild losses around 1.1465 during the early Asian session on Thursday. The US Dollar (USD) edges higher against the Euro (EUR) on a hawkish Federal Reserve (Fed) rate hold.

item.title: Yemen's Houthis reportedly considering fees for ships sailing through Red Sea
item.description: Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi rebels are considering imposing fees on commercial ships sailing through the southern Red Sea, Reuters reported on Wednesday. This development came a week after the Houthi declared a naval blockade on Saudi Arabia.

item.title: US President Donald Trump says US will strike Iran hard
item.description: US President Donald Trump said that he will order heavy strikes on Iran in retaliation for its “surprise attack” on US forces overnight, Bloomberg reported on Wednesday.

item.title: Gold rebounds to near $4,100 as Fed leaves interest rates unchanged
item.description: Gold price (XAU/USD) rebounds to around $4,095 during the early Asian session on Thursday.

item.title: GBP/JPY Price Forecast: Bulls reclaim 218.00 as RSI improves
item.description: The GBP/JPY advances by over 0.30%, rising above 218.00, as risk appetite improves amid overall US Dollar weakness following the Federal Reserve's monetary policy decision. The pair trades near 218.50 after hitting a low of the day (LOD) of 217.16.

item.title: A Fed hold, a Warsh non-answer, and one day of cover for the Japanese Yen
item.description: The Federal Reserve (Fed) held its target range at 3.50% to 3.75% for a fifth consecutive meeting at 18:00 GMT, and the pair did what a market short the Yen against a 1.00% policy rate does when a hike it partly paid for fails to arrive.

item.title: Forex Today: US Dollar tumbles after divided Fed hold, Oil surges on Middle East escalation
item.description: The US Dollar (USD) falls sharply during the American session on Wednesday after the Federal Reserve (Fed) left interest rates unchanged. The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) maintained the federal funds target range at 3.50%–3.75% in a divided 9–3 vote.

item.title: Silver holds firm as Dollar slides after split Fed decision
item.description: Silver price clings to gains on Wednesday late in the North American session, as the Federal Reserve held rates unchanged, which, instead of strengthening the Dollar, weakened it, while US Treasury yields spiked. The XAG/USD trades at $57.17, barely unchanged.

item.title: No soft target: Warsh vows to return inflation to 2%
item.description: The Fed left interest rates unchanged at 3.50%-3.75%, but the decision carried a distinctly hawkish edge as three officials voted for an immediate 25-basis-point increase.

item.title: WTI remains muted after Fed hold
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) Oil stayed muted near $83 per barrel following the Federal Reserve's (Fed) decision to hold interest rates constant on Wednesday afternoon. The price consolidation comes after recovering sharply from an intraday low near $78.90.

item.title: The Canadian Dollar waited for the Fed and got paid
item.description: The Federal Reserve held its target range at 3.50% to 3.75% at 18:00 GMT on a 9-3 vote, with three voting members preferring an immediate quarter-point increase, and USD/CAD fell out of a session-long range to print its low just beneath 1.4050.

item.title: British Pound Sterling rents a rally it has to pay for in the morning
item.description: The Federal Reserve (Fed) held its target range at 3.50% to 3.75% at 18:00 GMT on a 9-3 vote, with three voting members preferring an immediate quarter-point increase, and Sterling rallied through the 1.3300 shelf it lost last week to trade just above 1.3350. None of that is a British story.

item.title: Dow Jones Industrial Average gets its rate relief and cannot hold it
item.description: The Federal Reserve (Fed) held its target range at 3.50% to 3.75% at 18:00 GMT on a 9-3 vote, with three voting members preferring an immediate quarter-point increase.

item.title: The US Dollar Index discovers that a vote record is not a reaction function
item.description: The Federal Reserve held its target range at 3.50% to 3.75% at 18:00 GMT on a 9-3 vote, with three voting members preferring an immediate quarter-point increase. Previews had that configuration as the hawkish tail, the outcome that would bid the Dollar and punish risk assets.

item.title: Fed's Warsh: We will deliver the 2% target
item.description: At the post-meeting press conference, Fed Chair Kevin Warsh explains why policymakers decided to keep interest rates unchanged after the July meeting and takes questions from reporters about the decision.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar rebounds after Fed hold
item.description: NZD/USD trades higher near the 0.5790 area on Wednesday, reversing its earlier decline as the US Dollar (USD) weakens sharply following the Federal Reserve’s (Fed) monetary policy announcement.

item.title: Japanese Yen gains after hawkish Fed hold
item.description: USD/JPY trades near the 163.60 area on Wednesday, recovering from its immediate post-announcement decline as investors assess a generally hawkish Federal Reserve (Fed) monetary policy decision.

item.title: Australian Dollar trims losses after Fed holds
item.description: The Aussie Dollar trimmed some of its earlier losses after the Federal Reserve kept rates steady, by a 9 to 3 vote, with three dissenters who supported a 25-basis-point rate hike. The AUD/USD trades at around 0.6950, down 0.32%.

item.title: Euro rises despite Fed hawkish hold, eyes on Warsh’s speech
item.description: The shared currency surged after the Federal Reserve (Fed) kept rates steady by a 9 to 3 vote. Three dissenters supported a 25-basis-point rate hike. The EUR/USD trades in a volatile fashion above 1.1420, up 0.3%.

item.title: Gold surges after Fed holds as hawkish dissent fuels volatility
item.description: Gold price rises during the North American session after the Federal Reserve (Fed) decided to hold rates unchanged, with a 9-3 vote split, as three members of the FOMC opted to increase the fed funds rate by 25 basis points.

item.title: Mexican Peso tumbles as Gulf War escalation weighs on mood, Fed eyed
item.description: The Mexican Peso loses ground against the US Dollar on Wednesday as risk appetite turns sour amid the escalation of the Gulf War, while traders await the Federal Reserve’s (Fed) monetary policy decision. The USD/MXN trades at 17.51, up 0.47%.
